glossary.Occupational lung disease: Lung disease caused by breathing in harmful substances at work.
glossary.Occupational history: Detailed account of a patient's jobs, exposures and protective equipment, past and present.
glossary.Crackles: Clicking or crackling lung sounds heard with a stethoscope, as in fibrosis.
glossary.Wheeze: Whistling sound from air moving through narrowed airways.
glossary.Fibrosis: Replacement of normal tissue with scar tissue.
glossary.Late-onset asthma: Asthma that starts in adulthood rather than childhood.
glossary.Foam moulding: Industrial shaping of foam products, a source of isocyanate exposure.
glossary.Restrictive spirometry: Both FEV1 and FVC reduced with a normal or high ratio, as in stiff lungs.
glossary.FVC: Forced vital capacity: total air blown out after a full breath in.
glossary.FEV1: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second: air blown out in the first second.
glossary.Malignant pleural effusion: Fluid around the lung caused by cancer in the pleura.
glossary.Upper reference limit: The top of the normal range for a lab test.
glossary.Fluid protein: Amount of protein in pleural fluid; high levels suggest an exudate.
glossary.Coal workers' pneumoconiosis: Lung scarring from inhaling coal dust over many years.
glossary.Organic dust: Dust from living material such as mould, hay, grain or bird droppings.
glossary.Immune-mediated: Caused by the body's own immune response.
glossary.CT chest: Computed tomography scan giving detailed cross-sectional pictures of the chest.
glossary.Nodules: Small, round lesions seen on lung imaging.
glossary.Spirometry: A breathing test measuring how much and how fast air can be blown out.
glossary.TB testing: Tests for tuberculosis infection, such as interferon-gamma release assay or sputum testing.
glossary.Secondary care: Hospital-based specialist services that patients are referred to.
glossary.Steroids: Anti-inflammatory drugs such as prednisolone or inhaled corticosteroids.
glossary.Lung function: Measures of how well the lungs move air and transfer gas.
glossary.Particulates: Tiny solid particles in the air that can be breathed deep into the lung.
glossary.Airway hyperreactivity: Airways that narrow too easily in response to triggers.
glossary.Cytotoxic: Toxic to cells, directly damaging or killing them.
glossary.Mycobacterial: Caused by mycobacteria, the bacteria group that includes TB.
glossary.IgE-mediated: An immediate allergic reaction driven by IgE antibodies and mast cells.
glossary.Cell-mediated: An immune response driven by T cells rather than antibodies; delayed in onset.
glossary.Bronchoconstriction: Narrowing of the airways as their smooth muscle contracts.
glossary.Type IV hypersensitivity: Delayed, T-cell-mediated immune reaction occurring over days.
glossary.Antigen: A substance the immune system recognises and responds to.
glossary.Granulomatous inflammation: Inflammation forming granulomas: clusters of macrophages walling off a trigger.
